text: Breng Valley, also known as The Golden Crown of Kashmir, is situated in the Anantnag district of the Indian union territory of Jammu and Kashmir. The valley is named after the rivulet Brengi, which is a right-bank tributary of the Jhelum River. It extends over 40 km on either side of the Brengi and Kokernag, which serves as the central point of the valley and is home to the renowned Kokernag Garden. The valley has been lauded by the Kashmiri Sufi saint Sheikh Noor-u-din Wali, who referred to it as Breng Gov Sonsun Preng, meaning the Breng Valley is a Golden Crown. Located along the banks of the Brengi River, the valley is encircled by mountains that are part of the Pir Panjal range. It provides access routes to the Wardwan Valley via Margan Top and to Kishtwar via Sinthon Top. This article related to a location in Jammu and Kashmir is a stub.
